claims.text: Helm is a graduated Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) project.
Helm charts are directories of templated YAML manifests, a `values.yaml` file of default inputs, and metadata.
The `helm` CLI renders chart templates using Go template syntax and either installs the resulting manifests into a cluster as a release or prints them to stdout.
Helm charts are distributed through Helm repositories and indexed publicly on Artifact Hub.
Helm is open source under the Apache License 2.0.
The Helm project does not ship a commercial tier.
The Pulumi Registry includes providers for AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Kubernetes, Datadog, Cloudflare, GitHub, and Auth0.
Pulumi supports YAML and HCL as authoring languages in addition to general-purpose languages.
In Pulumi, resource ordering is derived from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind, defined in helm/helm pkg/release/v1/util/kind_sorter.go.
Helm chart authors can't declare dependencies between resources or subcharts, except through hook weights.
Pulumi state is managed by Pulumi Cloud by default; self-managed backends include Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, and local files.
Helm stores release metadata as Secrets (or ConfigMaps) inside the target Kubernetes cluster.
Failed Pulumi updates leave the stack in a partially-updated state; `pulumi up` reconciles toward desired state and `pulumi refresh` detects drift.
`helm rollback` restores a release to a previous revision recorded in release history.
Pulumi Automation API is a programmatic SDK in every supported Pulumi language for embedding `up`, `preview`, and `destroy` in a host application.
The Helm SDK is available in Go only; other languages must shell out to the `helm` CLI.
Pulumi Policies is open source, with rules in Python, TypeScript, or Open Policy Agent Rego.
Pulumi Cloud adds centralized policy management, and the Enterprise edition adds Pulumi-maintained policy packs for CIS, PCI DSS, HITRUST, and NIST.
Helm has no native policy engine; policy is typically delegated to Kubernetes admission controllers such as Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper.
Pulumi is open source under the Apache License 2.0.
Helm doesn't let a chart author declare that one resource depends on another.
The Helm docs state: "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's install order is a hardcoded list of Kubernetes kinds in the Helm source, beginning with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with any kind not on the list (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-ordered list in reverse.
Helm sends the sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
Helm chart dependencies don't change resource ordering: a subchart's objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind along with everything else.
A Helm chart can't express "install the database subchart before the application subchart" or "start this Deployment after that Job completes."
Helm workarounds for ordering are chart hooks ordered with `helm.sh/hook-weight` annotations, whose resources Helm doesn't manage as part of the release.
Native sequencing for resources and subcharts has been proposed in Helm HIP-0025, which is still a draft.
In Pulumi, passing one resource's output into another, or setting the `dependsOn` resource option, creates an edge in the dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating the resources that depend on it, and deploys independent resources in parallel.
Pulumi deletes follow the dependency graph in reverse.

Pulumi's `helm.v4.Chart` supports the `config.kubernetes.io/depends-on` annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and `dependsOn` on the chart for dependencies on resources outside it.
Pulumi updates are faster than a strict serial sequence because independent resources deploy in parallel.
Helm manages Kubernetes resources only.
Helm records each install or upgrade as a numbered release revision, and `helm rollback` restores a prior revision.
Pulumi runs through the local CLI, programmatically through the Automation API, or remotely through Pulumi Deployments.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated, and you roll forward by reverting program code and running `pulumi up`.
Helm and Pulumi are commonly used in combination rather than as substitutes.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm together.
Charts can be installed through Pulumi's `helm.v4.Chart` or `helm.v3.Release`.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after its dependencies.
Resource outputs flow into a Helm chart's `values` input as typed Pulumi outputs.
The FAQ page contains a section titled "What's the difference between `helm.Chart` and `helm.Release`?" with anchor #whats-the-difference-between-helmchart-and-helmrelease.
Pulumi creates and deletes resources in dependency order, with each resource ready before the ones that depend on it, rather than in a fixed order by kind.
There are three common ways to adopt Pulumi alongside or in place of Helm.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program via `helm.v4.Chart` or `helm.v3.Release` is the most common adoption pattern.
Charts can be converted to native Pulumi code by rendering them with `helm template` and converting the YAML with `pulumi convert --from kubernetes`.
`pulumi import` and the `import` resource option import existing in-cluster resources and generate the corresponding code.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider exposes Helm charts as first-class resources through `helm.v4.Chart` and `helm.v3.Release`, and can pull charts from any Helm repository (public or private).

`helm.v4.Chart` renders chart templates locally and registers each Kubernetes object the chart produces as an individual Pulumi resource, so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state.
`helm.v3.Release` uses the embedded Helm SDK and creates a real Helm release in the cluster, preserving chart hooks, post-rendering, and release history.

Helm merges the objects from a chart and all of its dependencies into a single set, sorts them by Kubernetes kind, and applies them in that order, so declaring a subchart as a dependency doesn't make it install first.
Ordering within a Helm release requires chart hooks with hook weights or logic in the application itself.
The Pulumi `values` input for a Helm chart accepts the same shape as a `values.yaml` file but lets each leaf be a Pulumi output; Pulumi installs the chart after the resources it depends on.
Pulumi can replace Helm by converting charts to native Pulumi code, and `pulumi convert --from kubernetes` converts rendered chart YAML to native Pulumi code.
